# Was Rackspace Spot hacked?

**Reported.** Reportedly yes: Rackspace's customer notice, quoted by BleepingComputer, says leaked credentials let someone into Spot on Nov 17, and a Spot team member said the same on Spot's GitHub forum. No Rackspace-hosted statement yet.

Incident: Rackspace Spot breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Rackspace Spot outage and the Rackspace Spot Kubernetes breach. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 6:34 PM ET.

Picture: Rackspace logo (used for identification; Rackspace is not affiliated with isitahack.com). Image: Rackspace Technology logo, trademark of Rackspace, public domain on Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rackspace_Technology.svg).

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Rackspace, Platform9, BleepingComputer, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 6:34 PM ET: **A Spot team member wrote on Spot's GitHub forum that an observability system was breached via a compromised credential; still Reported.** New source s004 (Tier 4): Rackspace Spot's GitHub Discussions thread 'Update On Spot Outage', Nov 20, where a Spot team member said an observability system was breached using a compromised credential and that intrusive infrastructure changes caused the extended outage, then gave a 9am Pacific Nov 21 restoration estimate. Added c012 (Reported), t005 and t006; added s004 to c003, c004 and c011. c001 stays Reported: a forum post is Tier 4 and not a Rackspace-hosted statement. c011 stays Not established: no published incident report, and whose credential and how it leaked are unknown. Rackspace release notes and status page unchanged (sign-up restriction notice still pinned, no breach mention). Other new coverage (Mezha, infonewscyber.fr) rewrites BleepingComputer, same independence group; no second independent outlet. BleepingComputer read through a search tool. Reddit not checked: access blocked. Staleness check done: q001 answer and incident.json known/not_known refreshed. Privacy check done: no names, usernames or handles.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Rackspace Spot runs customers' Kubernetes clusters, and the admin console was down for days. Rackspace reportedly says some customer organizations were affected. The number is unknown.
- Who is affected: Organizations that run workloads on Rackspace Spot. Rackspace reportedly told affected customers to reissue Spot API tokens, replace refresh tokens, download new kubeconfig files and rotate credentials in cluster Secrets. Other customers should watch Rackspace's notices.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 17 | Reported access window (UTC) | About 00:20 to 22:00 UTC, per the notice |
| Nov 21 | Service reportedly restored | Per BleepingComputer; console was down for days |
| Nov 25 | New sign-ups restricted until | 17:00 UTC, on Rackspace's status page |

### Known so far

- Rackspace's release notes list a November 2026 fix that closed a network exposure on Spot worker nodes as part of security hardening.
- Rackspace's Spot status page says new sign-ups are restricted until Nov 25, 17:00 UTC after recent system maintenance.

### Not known yet

- Whether Rackspace itself has confirmed the breach on a page it hosts. Reports rely on a customer notice and a Spot team member's forum post.
- Whether customer data or Secrets were actually read or misused, not just readable.
- How many customers were affected.
- Whose credential was used, how it leaked, what the breached observability system is, and who used it.
- Whether the full restoration Nov 21 is confirmed by Rackspace on its own pages.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the latest check (2026-11-21T18:34:58-05:00).

- Rackspace's customer notice, or any statement about a breach, on a page Rackspace hosts. The Spot release notes and status page do not mention one.
- A second outlet confirming BleepingComputer's report.
- A Rackspace incident report or post-mortem saying how the credentials leaked. A Spot team member's forum post says an observability system was breached using a compromised credential, but that is not an incident report.
- Any statement on how many customers were affected or whether data was stolen or misused.
- Any government or independent analysis naming the attacker, or any claim of responsibility or ransom reported by press. We did not visit leak sites or trackers.
- A Rackspace-hosted announcement that Spot service was fully restored.
